intents.title: ASR Fundamentals & Pipeline
patterns: how does speech to text work
how do computers understand human speech
how does voice recognition convert audio to text
basics of speech to text systems
how does asr convert speech into text
responses:
**Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR)**—also called Speech-to-Text (STT)—converts spoken audio waveforms into written text.

A modern ASR pipeline has **4 core stages**:
1. **Audio Preprocessing**: Resampling (typically 16 kHz mono PCM), Voice Activity Detection (VAD), and noise suppression.
2. **Feature Extraction**: Converting waveforms via Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) into **80-channel Log-Mel Spectrograms** or **MFCCs**.
3. **Acoustic / End-to-End Neural Model**: Mapping audio frames to subword tokens using **Conformer**, **Whisper (Transformer)**, **Wav2Vec 2.0**, or **RNN-Transducer (RNN-T)**.
4. **Decoding & Language Modeling**: Beam search, CTC prefix decoding, or shallow fusion with an external Language Model to output punctuated text.

intents.title: Audio Features (MFCC & Spectrograms)
patterns: stft short time fourier transform audio
how is audio converted into features
windowing and framing in speech processing
why use mel scale in audio
responses:
**Audio Feature Extraction** transforms raw 1D waveforms into 2D time-frequency representations aligned with human pitch perception:

- **Framing & Windowing**: 16 kHz audio is sliced into **25 ms frames** with a **10 ms hop (stride)** using a Hann/Hamming window.
- **STFT**: Computes the frequency magnitude spectrum per frame.
- **Log-Mel Spectrogram**: Applies **80 or 128 triangular Mel-filterbanks** (logarithmically spaced to match the human cochlea) + log compression. Standard input for **Whisper** and **Conformer**.
- **MFCCs**: Applies Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to decorrelate log-mel filterbanks (classic GMM-HMM feature).
- **Learned CNN Encoders**: Self-supervised models like **Wav2Vec 2.0** learn features directly from raw 16 kHz waveforms using multi-layer 1D convolutions.

intents.title: Hybrid Acoustic/Language Models
patterns: what is a language model in asr
difference between acoustic model and language model
hybrid dnn hmm vs end to end asr
how do language models improve speech recognition
shallow fusion and beam search decoding
responses:
Classical ASR formulates transcription via **Bayes' Rule**, finding word sequence $W^*$ maximizing $P(X|W) \cdot P(W)$:

- **Acoustic Model $P(X|W)$**: Predicts phonetic state probabilities (senones/phonemes) from acoustic frames $X$ (e.g., GMM-HMM, Kaldi TDNN-HMM).
- **Pronunciation Lexicon**: Maps words to phoneme sequences (`RECOGNIZE -> R EH K AH G N AY Z`).
- **Language Model $P(W)$**: Scores word sequence likelihood via n-grams or neural LMs to disambiguate homophones like *"recognize speech"* vs. *"wreck a nice beach"*.

Modern **End-to-End (E2E) ASR** merges all three components into one neural network outputting subword tokens directly!

intents.title: CTC, RNN-T & Conformer Architectures
patterns: compare ctc rnnt and attention models
how does ctc blank token work
best architecture for real time streaming asr
responses:
Modern End-to-End ASR uses **3 alignment architectures** paired with a **Conformer** encoder:

1. **CTC (Connectionist Temporal Classification)**: Uses a `<blank>` symbol and dynamic programming to align audio frames to text without frame-level labels. Fast & non-autoregressive, but assumes output tokens are conditionally independent.
2. **RNN-Transducer (RNN-T)**: Joins an Acoustic Encoder + Prediction Network + Joint Network. Supports **low-latency streaming** without CTC's independence assumption (used in on-device ASR & NVIDIA Parakeet).
3. **Attention Encoder-Decoder (AED / Whisper)**: Cross-attends over encoded audio frames autoregressively—delivering top offline accuracy, capitalization, and punctuation.
4. **Conformer Backbone**: Combines **Multi-Head Self-Attention** (global context) + **Depthwise Convolution** (local phonetic detail) inside a Macaron feed-forward block.

intents.title: OpenAI Whisper & Speech Foundation Models
responses:
**OpenAI Whisper** is a weakly-supervised Transformer Encoder-Decoder trained on **680k–5M hours** of multilingual & multitask web audio:

- **Frontend**: Resamples audio to 16 kHz, pads/trims to 30s windows, computes **80/128-channel Log-Mel Spectrograms**, and downsamples 2x via two 1D Conv layers + GELU.
- **Multitask Decoder Tokens**: Uses control tokens (`<|startoftranscript|>`, `<|lang|>`, `<|transcribe|>`, `<|translate|>`, `<|timestamps|>`) so a single model handles ASR, language ID, voice translation, and word timestamps.
- **Deployment Tips**:
  - Use **Faster-Whisper (CTranslate2 INT8)** or **Whisper-large-v3-turbo** (4 decoder layers instead of 32) for 4x–6x speedups.
  - Pre-filter silence with **Silero VAD** to prevent decoder looping/hallucinations!

intents.title: Self-Supervised Speech (Wav2Vec 2.0 & HuBERT)
patterns: how does wav2vec 2.0 differ from whisper
how does wav2vec 2.0 learn from raw audio
train asr with little labeled data
responses:
**Self-Supervised Speech Models** (**Wav2Vec 2.0**, **HuBERT**, **WavLM**, **Meta MMS**) pre-train on massive **unlabeled raw audio** and fine-tune with minimal labeled data (even 10 minutes!):

- **Wav2Vec 2.0**: Encodes raw 16 kHz PCM waveforms with a 7-layer CNN, masks latent spans, and trains via contrastive loss over quantized speech units.
- **HuBERT**: Uses iterative k-means clustering on MFCC/latent features to create discrete acoustic targets for masked prediction.
- **WavLM**: Adds masked speech denoising during pre-training, achieving top results on **speaker diarization** and noisy ASR.
- **Whisper vs. Wav2Vec 2.0**: Whisper is trained with weak supervision (audio+transcripts) as Seq2Seq; Wav2Vec 2.0 is self-supervised on unlabeled audio and usually fine-tuned with a **CTC head**.

intents.title: Word Error Rate (WER) & CER Evaluation
patterns: how do you calculate word error rate
how to evaluate speech recognition accuracy
responses:
**Word Error Rate (WER)** is the gold-standard accuracy metric for Automatic Speech Recognition, computed via **Levenshtein Edit Distance** at the word level:

`WER = (Substitutions + Deletions + Insertions) / Reference_Words × 100%`

- **Substitutions ($S$)**: Misrecognized word (`"speech"` → `"beach"`)
- **Deletions ($D$)**: Omitted reference word
- **Insertions ($I$)**: Extra hallucinated word (note: because of insertions, WER can exceed 100%!)
- **CER (Character Error Rate)**: Computes edit distance over characters—preferred for Mandarin, Japanese, or agglutinative languages.

👉 Open the **WER Evaluator** tab at the top of this app to run live Levenshtein word alignments right now!

intents.title: VAD, Speaker Diarization & Noise Robustness
responses:
Production voice pipelines surround ASR with **VAD, Diarization, and Noise Robustness**:

- **Voice Activity Detection (VAD)**: Classifies 10–30 ms audio chunks into speech vs. non-speech (**Silero VAD**, **WebRTC VAD**). Essential for turn endpointing in voice chatbots and preventing Whisper hallucinations during silence.
- **Speaker Diarization ("Who spoke when?")**: Combines VAD + neural speaker embeddings (**ECAPA-TDNN / pyannote.audio**) + spectral clustering to assign speaker labels (`Speaker A`, `Speaker B`) to ASR timestamps.
- **Noise Robustness**: Achieved via **SpecAugment** (masking time/frequency bands during training), multi-condition room simulator data (RIRs + MUSAN noise), and microphone array beamforming.

intents.title: ASR Datasets & Python Training Pipeline
patterns: what datasets are used to train asr
how to train an asr model in python
how do you fine tune an asr model in python
what is specaugment in asr training
how was this chatbot trained in python
python training part of this chatbot
responses:
**ASR Datasets & Python Training Ecosystem**:

- **Standard Datasets**: **LibriSpeech** (960h English audiobooks), **Mozilla Common Voice** (100+ languages), **GigaSpeech** (10,000h multi-domain), **VoxPopuli**, and **FLEURS**.
- **Python Frameworks**: Hugging Face `transformers`, **SpeechBrain**, **ESPnet**, **NVIDIA NeMo**, `torchaudio`, and `librosa`.
- **SpecAugment**: Masks random mel-frequency channels and time steps directly on spectrograms during Python training to boost generalization.
- **How This Chatbot Was Trained**: Run `npm run train` (`python3 training/train_chatbot.py`)! Python extracts Sublinear TF-IDF Word (1–2) + Character (3–4) n-grams and fits an L2-regularized Multi-Class Softmax classifier, exporting weights to `src/model/chatbot_model.json` for fast JavaScript edge inference.

intents.title: Web Speech API & Real-Time JS Voice Bots
patterns: how does web speech api work in browsers
how does web speech api work in javascript
how to build a voice chatbot in javascript
how do real time voice chatbots reduce latency
how do voice agents achieve sub 500ms latency
voice chatbot architecture stt llm tts
how does microphone input work in this app
responses:
**Real-Time JavaScript Voice Chatbots** run a tight **3-stage loop (`ASR → NLP → TTS`)**:

1. **Live Browser ASR (`SpeechRecognition` + Web Audio API)**: Streams microphone audio with `interimResults = true` to show partial transcripts in real time, while `AudioContext + AnalyserNode` renders live frequency bars.
2. **Low-Latency NLP Inference**: Our JavaScript backend (`src/inference.js`) executes matrix-vector Softmax inference over the Python-trained weights in **<1 ms**, logging transcripts and confidence scores to SQLite/D1.
3. **Voice Output (`speechSynthesis`)**: Speaks bot answers aloud with toggleable auto-voice and instant barge-in interruption whenever you start speaking again!
